## 1. What this application is

`u2giants/shared-db` is the canonical repository for **one** Supabase PostgreSQL database shared by five separate applications, each in its own repo:

| App | What it is | Status | Repo |
|---|---|---|---|
| PopDAM | digital asset management | live | `u2giants/popdam3` |
| PopCRM | customer relationship management | live | `u2giants/popcrm-web` |
| DesignFlow PLM ("dflow") | product lifecycle management | live | `popcre/designflow-*` (six repos) |
| PopPIM | product information management | in development | `u2giants/poppim-web` |
| monitor | Synology NAS monitoring | live | `u2giants/synology-monitor` |

Schema changes are authored here, proved on **preview** (`rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel`), then promoted to **production** (`qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`). There is no "just my app" change — one bad migration breaks all five.

**Who works here:** AI sessions (Claude, Codex, GLM, Grok, Kimi, Qwen), frequently **3–7 at once**, sometimes in the same working copy. The owner, **Albert Hazan**, is a business owner and **explicitly not a programmer** — AI sessions are the entire engineering department. **Controls must be mechanical; anything relying on a human remembering a written rule will not happen.** That fact drives every decision below.

**Branch model:** branch + PR, and **the AI merges its own PRs** (specific to `shared-db`).
**The repo is PUBLIC.** That is load-bearing for this workstream.

## 2. What we set out to do, and why

**In business terms:** the file that tracks who needs what done on the shared database is a 3,837-line Markdown document that several AI sessions edit simultaneously. It is a hand-built imitation of an issue tracker. GitHub already provides a real one. Move the work items there.

**What triggered it.** Albert asked whether the 8 open handoff files should become Issues. Answering that required separating two things that had been conflated:

- **Handoff files** are ~10-page briefings for the next worker. **Not** tickets. They stay as files.
- **The coordinator queue** (`COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md`) *is* a ticket system, badly reimplemented. **That** is what moves.

He then chose **public** Issues over a private repo, having been told the queue contains licensor names, customer data problems and internal incident write-ups.

**The measured case for moving.** The queue grew **0 → 68 items in six days and has never once shrunk**. `docs/intake-archive/` **does not exist**, so its retention rule has never fired. Two of its rules **deadlock**: retention requires archiving blocks that a CI check requires stay present. The file itself instructs readers that no document wins by name or date and that facts must be re-derived from `git`/`gh` — an admission it is not trustworthy.

2. **My second answer — repoint the check at Issues instead of deleting it — was also wrong, and the reason it was wrong is the useful part.** I preferred it partly because *it needed no owner decision*. That was the tell: I was optimising to avoid asking Albert, when §6.7 rule 3 exists precisely to make that ask mandatory. Satisfying the rule by the letter (keep the context name) while changing the check from offline-deterministic to online-best-effort is routing around a control. **GLM argued for going to Albert and I changed position.** Repointing survives only as the documented fallback if he says no (plan §7 Q1).

3. **My scrub step said "do not do it by eye" and then supplied no tool.** That is an eye-scan with extra words, in a repo whose entire philosophy is that human-performed rules do not happen. GLM refused to let it stand and was right. It is now a real script (plan step 2).

4. **I had steps 5 and 8 in the wrong order.** The original updated the skills *after* emptying the queue file. GLM traced the consequence: a machine still running the old skill appends to the emptied pointer file and **rebuilds its body**, live, mid-migration, with no alarm — the exact failure the plan exists to prevent. **Skills propagate to every machine first.**

5. **"One issue per block" would have produced four issues for one thing.** The Disney OPA item spans four blocks (`COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md:682`, `:776`, `:821`, `:2946`). Now one issue per **work item**.

6. **My step-9 verification gate was false-green.** It searched for `INTAKE QUEUE`, `TAKEN OVER` and `B2.2` — none of which appear in the two places the rules are actually restated (see §5B). The gate would have passed with the rules fully alive. Same disease as the broken check being retired.

7. **`ai-glm ask` aborted with "review session CHANGED the working tree".** Alarming, and benign: the wrapper snapshots `git status` before and after, and its **own round-1 report** under `.ai/reviews/` is a new untracked file, so the next turn trips on it. **No tracked file changed and GLM edited nothing** — verified before continuing. Recovery: `ai-glm abort <session>` then re-ask; the session keeps its context. **Do not panic-revert on this message; check `git status` first.**

8. **GLM was confidently wrong once, and the shape is the lesson.** It claimed `gh issue list --label` returns empty in this repo, citing `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md:3019`, and built two objections on it. Tested live: it works — `--label coordinator-marker` correctly returned issue #473. It had quoted a **document** as evidence, in a review whose entire subject is that this repo trusts documents over the repo. Both objections withdrawn. **Verify a reviewer's citations the same way you would verify a document's.**

## 5. Root causes and key findings

**A. The check everyone treats as a control is much smaller than its name.** `Backlog / queue sync` only ever verified that each of the **14 backlog items** (`B1`–`B14` in `HANDOFF.md ## BACKLOG`) has a reference in the queue. It **never once looked at the 67 queue items** that are the actual sprawl. It is also already false-passing: its `B_REFERENCE` regex matches a bare number anywhere in prose rather than requiring a real heading. **A small, broken check with a big name.** This reframing is what settled the repoint-vs-remove argument.

**B. Two live backlog items are instructions to rebuild exactly what this plan removes.** This is the single most important thing to carry forward:
- `HANDOFF.md:1850` — *"B10 — Coordinator intake lifecycle/retention is MANUAL; CI could enforce it (NOT implemented)"*
- `HANDOFF.md:1943` — *"B13 — CI check: every BACKLOG `B<n>` should have a `REQUEST QUEUE` entry (DONE)"*

A faithful future session reading B10 rebuilds the queue. **Step 9 must rewrite or close both**, and its gate now searches for them.

**C. ⚠️ THE TWO LIVE PLANS COLLIDE OVER ONE FILE.** `plan_dispatch-collision-hardening.md` (Phase A merged, Phases B and C open) and this plan have opposite fates for `scripts/check-backlog-queue-sync.mjs`:
- That plan's **§4 item 4** (`:177`) defers *fixing* it and says the fix is "tracked in the `REQUEST QUEUE`" — a queue this plan deletes.
- That plan's **§10 "must stay green"** list (`:950–951`) runs the script and its tests. **This plan's step 7b deletes both.** A Phase B or C session running that list verbatim would hit a missing file and reasonably read it as its own breakage.

**Recorded in BOTH plans this session** (as `D-A11` in the collision plan, and constraint 9 in this one). **Whichever plan reaches the conflict first updates the other in the same PR.** Neither may quietly win.

**D. The silent-loss door is at step 1, not step 6, and the mapping file cannot see it.** A block misclassified NOISE or ALREADY-DONE never reaches the creation script, and a mapping file only records what the script was given — "nothing was lost from the set it saw" is circular. The plan now requires arithmetic: `migrated + closed-with-reason + noise-with-justification == total blocks`.

**E. There is no "local, non-published" location inside a public repo.** GLM proposed keeping the dead-end knowledge in a `docs/intake-archive/` that is *"preserved without publishing"*. In a public repo a committed file is published exactly as an issue is. GLM conceded. The underlying point stands and is now plan open question **Q2**: dead-end content otherwise survives only in old commits, where nobody looks.

**F. `gh issue list --label` works here.** Verified live 2026-08-07. Load-bearing for the migration script's idempotency.

## 7. Constraints and gotchas in force

1. **Branch + PR, and you merge it yourself.** Never commit to `main` directly.
2. **Commit identity must be `Albert Hazan <u2giants@users.noreply.github.com>`.** Check `git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT` **before** your first commit — 231 wrong-identity commits already reached shared branches and cannot be fixed.
3. **Never weaken branch protection without a named owner instruction** — `AGENTS.md:1081`. This is the rule my first draft broke.
4. **Branch protection: `strict: true`, six required contexts, `enforce_admins: true`.** `main` moves often; expect `gh pr update-branch`. It happened twice today.
5. **`shared-db` is PUBLIC.** A committed file is published exactly as an issue is. **Do not create issues or labels without asking Albert.**
6. **Publishing is one-way** — content can be indexed and cached even if deleted afterwards.
7. **You may share this checkout with other live sessions.** Before opening a PR run `git diff origin/main --stat` and confirm it lists only your files. **Never `git add -A`**; stage explicit paths. Uncommitted changes you did not make are another session's live work.
8. **Do not delete `.ai/deepseek-sessions/` or `.ai/reviews/`.**
9. **No band-aids, no silent failures.** Every fallback must be loud.
10. **Windows line endings:** `.mjs`/`.md` edits warn `LF will be replaced by CRLF`. Harmless; do not "fix" it, do not reformat whole files.
11. **`bash scripts/check-sql.sh` and `bash bin/ai-install-skills` do not run on this machine** — they die at `set -o pipefail` because of CRLF line endings. They run fine in CI on Linux. **Do not "fix" the scripts**; backlog item B1 owns the line endings. For skills, copy the file and verify with `Get-FileHash`.
12. **The `ai-glm` wrapper trips on its own report file** — see §4.7. Check `git status` before believing it.
13. **The stranded-CI-run trap.** During a GitHub Actions outage a required check can sit at `queued` for hours; GitHub refuses to cancel it while still reporting it queued, so the PR is BLOCKED forever. `gh run rerun` and close/reopen both fail. **Only moving the SHA frees it:** `git commit --allow-empty -m "ci: re-trigger" && git push`. Did not occur today; CI was healthy.

**1. Could a brand-new developer with no project knowledge pick up where I left off and not skip a beat?** **Yes.** §1 defines the five apps, both databases, the branch model, and the public-repo fact that drives the whole workstream. §3 gives both merged PRs, states plainly that nothing is executed and nothing published, and names the two unasked owner gates. §6 orders the next steps and puts the coordinator-marker check *before* step 1, which is where a newcomer would otherwise walk straight into a stop condition. *Gap found during the audit and fixed:* the first draft opened at step 1 without mentioning issue #473 — a fresh session following the orchestrator skill would have hit an open marker on its first command with no explanation.

**2. Could they continue as effectively as I can right now?** **Yes.** §4 records eight dead ends, including **two where I was wrong and changed position** (deleting protection, then repointing to avoid asking the owner) with the reasoning that moved me, one where the tooling produced an alarming false alarm, and one where the reviewer was confidently wrong with the method error that caused it. §5 records six findings with `file:line`, including the cross-plan collision that neither plan knew about until today. §9 dates eight decisions. *Gap found and fixed:* the first draft did not say that a warm GLM session already holds the full review context — a newcomer would have started a fresh one, lost every conclusion, and paid full price for cached context. Now in §8 and in the plan's constraints.

**3.
